Title: System Architecture Design
Description: Design the AI agents and other services needed to fulfil the user stories requirements.

Title: Data contracts
Description: Shared Pydantic models every module passes to each other (architecture §4). Depends on: F0.
Acceptance criteria:
• RequestContext, RiskAssessment, TaskPlan, AgentResult, ActionCommand, Receipt and AuditEvent exist in backend/app/schemas/
• Every field in architecture §4 and §6.3 is present and typed; enums use Literal types
• AgentResult.status includes needs_clarification with a question field
• SSE event models cover status, answer (with sections[]), action_required, done and error
• Unit tests build one valid and one invalid example of each model
• Merged in one PR, approved by all developers

How to build:
1. Copy each JSON example from architecture §4 into a Pydantic model
2. Add the SSE event models next to the existing ones in schemas/chat.py
3. Write a round-trip test per model
4. Open one PR and get all developers to review

Title: Operational database and synthetic seed
Description: Business tables with RLS, plus fake data for Alex, Michelle and David. Depends on: F0.
Acceptance criteria:
• Schemas banking, compliance, rm, consent, conversation, actions, support, notify and events migrate cleanly on the hosted project
• RLS is enabled on every customer table; a signed-in customer reads only their own rows
• Seed includes Alex's card ending 4821, the $2,400 charge and the pending landlord transfer
• Seed includes Michelle's compliance case, requested documents and deadline
• Seed includes David's old and new RM, advisor working hours and an open request
• Synthetic data only; no service-role key in the app or browser
• Migration numbering rule is written in the README

How to build:
1. Write one migration per schema in backend/supabase/migrations/
2. Add RLS policies keyed on customer_id
3. Write a seed migration for the three personas
4. Test RLS by signing in as each persona and reading another persona's rows

Title: Audit Log Service
Description: Append-only, tamper-evident record of who did what. Depends on: F1, F2.
Acceptance criteria:
• audit.events can only be written through audit.record() (SECURITY DEFINER)
• UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE are revoked from all app roles
• Each row stores prev_hash and hash; editing a row breaks the chain and a check script detects it
• A generic trigger records insert/update/delete on audited business tables
• State changes write their audit row in the same transaction
• A failed audit write fails the request
• Events hold ids, enums and counts only, never user text or customer records

How to build:
1. Create the audit schema, table and record() function
2. Add the hash chain and a verify script
3. Attach the row trigger to business tables
4. Add a Python helper that batches events per request

Title: API Gateway Layer
Description: Entry point that checks who is calling and builds the RequestContext. Depends on: F1, F3.
Acceptance criteria:
• JWT is verified with cached JWKS; invalid or expired tokens get 401
• customer_id comes only from the JWT, never from the request body
• Guests get a guest principal with no customer_id
• Rate limit and payload size limit return stable error codes
• auth.session_started is recorded the first time a session_id is seen
• POST /auth/session-end records auth.session_ended
• Every request has a request_id passed to all modules

How to build:
1. Move JWT checks from core/auth.py into middleware
2. Build RequestContext and attach it to the request
3. Add the in-process token-bucket rate limit
4. Add the session-end endpoint and audit events

Title: Input Guardrail
Description: Rule-based check of every message before any AI runs. Depends on: F1.
Acceptance criteria:
• Returns a RiskAssessment for every message
• Never calls the LLM
• Card numbers, passwords, OTPs and NRIC are redacted and counted
• Lost card, shared secrets and human-support requests return fixed responses
• Guest asking about 'my balance' gets the log-in fixed response
• Fraud wording sets fraud_suspected and priority P0
• Shared privacy fixtures pass in backend and frontend; ordinary password-reset questions are unchanged

How to build:
1. Merge privacy.py and safety.py behind one guard() function
2. Add fraud wording rules and priority
3. Keep frontend lib/chatTools.js redaction in sync
4. Extend tests/fixtures/privacy-cases.json

Title: LLM Gateway
Description: One model client for the planner and all agents. Depends on: F1.
Acceptance criteria:
• Planner and agents all call the model through this client
• Prompts load by agent and version from prompts/<agent>/vN
• Output is parsed against a strict JSON schema
• Timeouts, limited retries and a per-request token budget are enforced
• Errors are reported, never replaced with a sample answer
• Model, tokens and latency are recorded per call with a trace span
• Released prompt versions are never edited; each new version has a prompt-log entry

How to build:
1. Wrap the existing services/llm.py call in a generic client
2. Extend services/prompts.py to load per-agent folders
3. Add timeout, retry and budget settings to core/config.py
4. Record token and latency in the trace tables

Title: Conversation Store
Description: Saves chats so follow-ups and returning customers keep context. Depends on: F2, F4, F5.
Acceptance criteria:
• Each turn is saved with redacted text only
• A follow-up in the same chat sees the earlier turns
• A signed-in customer can list and reopen only their own chats (RLS)
• Cases group the tasks from one conversation
• LangGraph checkpoints are stored here
• Guest sessions expire

How to build:
1. Create conversation.sessions, messages, cases and checkpoints
2. Save each turn after the guardrail
3. Load history at the start of each turn
4. Add an endpoint to list previous chats

Title: Knowledge Service
Description: Moves the article library into Supabase with full-text search. Depends on: F2.
Acceptance criteria:
• kb.articles, kb.sections and kb.facts exist with read-only RLS
• kb.search() returns ranked sections cited as article_id@vN#anchor
• Unrelated questions return no sections
• get_fact() returns exact fees, limits and rates
• knowledge.py reads from Supabase; today's answers still pass the offline evaluation
• External articles have reference_url, checked_on, review_due and an allowed domain

How to build:
1. Write the kb migration from knowledge-base-design.md
2. Move current in-memory articles into a content migration
3. Write the kb.search() SQL function
4. Point knowledge.py at the RPC and rerun the evaluation

Title: Authorisation & Consent Service
Description: One place that decides whether a read or action is allowed. Depends on: F2, F3.
Acceptance criteria:
• decide() returns allow, reasons and obligations (mask, require confirmation, require consent)
• Guests are denied all personal data
• An agent calling a tool outside its allow-list is denied
• card.unblock requires step-up (aal2)
• Auto vs confirm action types are listed in the policy rules
• has_consent() respects expiry and revocation
• Every decision writes a policy.decision audit event

How to build:
1. Write policy rules as Python in services/authorisation.py
2. Create consent.grants with RLS
3. Add has_consent()
4. Test each rule with allow and deny cases

Title: Customer Data Service
Description: The only way agents read customer records. Depends on: F2, F9.
Acceptance criteria:
• Functions exist for profile, accounts, transactions, credit cards, loans, compliance case, RM assignment, requests and free slots
• Every query filters by customer_id in code and runs with the user JWT so RLS applies
• Card numbers show last 4 only; account numbers and NRIC are masked
• Every call asks decide() first
• Every result returns a call_id the validator can check figures against
• Every call writes a data.read audit event
• No service-role key is used

How to build:
1. Create services/customer_data.py with one function per read
2. Add masking helpers
3. Return {call_id, data, as_of}
4. Write RLS tests per persona

Title: Action Service core
Description: run_action(): the single path for every change. Depends on: F3, F9.
Acceptance criteria:
• Confirm-type actions stop as proposed and send action_required
• Proposed commands expire after 5 minutes; an expired confirm executes nothing
• A repeated request or confirm returns the same receipt
• Policy is re-checked at confirm time
• Change, outbox row and audit event commit in one transaction
• Every executed action returns a receipt
• The model can never choose or call an executor directly
• POST /commands/{id}/confirm works

How to build:
1. Create actions.commands with idempotency_key
2. Write run_action() with the seven steps from architecture §5.7.3
3. Add the executor registry
4. Add the confirm endpoint

Title: Card and handoff executors
Description: Card blocking and passing a case to a person. Depends on: F11.
Acceptance criteria:
• Card block runs only after the customer confirms
• Allowed transitions are active → temporarily_blocked → active / cancelled; others are rejected
• Unblock and permanent cancel are staff-only
• Handoff includes a redacted case summary
• Only one open handoff per case and reason
• Handoff queue orders P0 first, then age
• RLS tests pass

How to build:
1. Write services/actions/cards.py
2. Write services/actions/handoffs.py and support.handoffs
3. Register both in the executor registry
4. Add a staff script to claim and close handoffs

Title: Appointment and records executors
Description: Bookings, consent and record updates. Depends on: F9, F11.
Acceptance criteria:
• A slot hold lasts 10 minutes
• Two bookings on the same slot cannot both succeed (exclusion constraint)
• Booking is confirmed only after the customer confirms
• Sharing a summary or agenda fails without an active consent grant
• Consent grants and revocations are written only here, each with a receipt
• Checklist update, agenda save and consent request run without confirmation

How to build:
1. Write services/actions/appointments.py and the booking table
2. Write services/actions/records.py
3. Register all types with their auto/confirm setting
4. Test double booking and missing consent

Title: Conversation Orchestrator
Description: Splits a message into tasks, runs agents and merges one reply. Depends on: F5, F6, F7, F16.
Acceptance criteria:
• Several issues in one message become separate tasks
• Clear single-intent messages are planned by rules without an LLM call
• Tasks are ordered P0 fraud > P1 security > P2 deadline > P3; guardrail flags override
• Independent tasks run in parallel with a timeout each
• Reply has one section per task in priority order
• Loan and fee sections get the disclaimer
• Conversation pauses for confirmation and resumes from the checkpoint
• A failed agent withholds only its own section
• Runs behind PIPELINE=v2; PIPELINE=v1 runs today's chatbot unchanged

How to build:
1. Add the PIPELINE setting
2. Build the LangGraph graph with plan, prioritise, dispatch, compose
3. Add the Postgres checkpointer and interrupt on proposed actions
4. Resume the graph from the confirm endpoint

Title: Response Validator
Description: Checks each section before it is shown. Depends on: F8, F10, F11, F14.
Acceptance criteria:
• Sections without valid sources are withheld
• Source ids exist and match the allowed scope
• Figures match kb.facts or a Customer Data result
• 'Blocked' / 'done' wording appears only with a receipt
• No secrets, URLs or prompt text leak
• Failure → section withheld, origin validation, needs_human=True and a handoff
• Other sections are still released

How to build:
1. Extend source_checks.py to run per section
2. Pass tool results and receipts into the validator
3. Create a handoff on failure
4. Add tests for each failure type

Title: Stub Agents
Description: Minimal version of each of the five agents for the user stories to build on. Depends on: F1, F6, F9.
Acceptance criteria:
• Everyday Banking, Fraud & Security, Compliance Review, Document Check and Relationship agents exist
• Each has a prompt v1 folder and a prompt-log entry
• Each has its tool allow-list from architecture §5.6
• Each returns a valid AgentResult from the real provider, never a fixed sample answer
• An out-of-scope request returns to the orchestrator
• The orchestrator can dispatch a task to every agent

How to build:
1. Create services/agents/ with one file per agent
2. Write a short v1 prompt per agent
3. Register agents and allow-lists
4. Add a live test that calls each agent once

Title: Local deployment
Description: Run the whole app locally with one command. Depends on: F4, F14.
Acceptance criteria:
• docker compose up starts web and api against the hosted Supabase project
• The chatbot works end to end in the browser
• Secrets come from .env only and are not baked into images or committed
• README explains how to start and stop it

How to build:
1. Write Dockerfiles for frontend and backend
2. Write docker-compose.yml with env_file
3. Document the steps in README

Title: Hardening and report evidence
Description: Check the foundation is safe and fast before persona work builds on it. Depends on: F1–F17.
Acceptance criteria:
• RLS checks pass for all three personas
• Audit hash chain verifies with no gaps
• Every request has trace spans per node, agent and tool
• Playwright smoke test of PIPELINE=v2 passes with the real provider
• Latency per request type is measured against the architecture budget
• Results and limitations are written up for the report

How to build:
1. Write RLS and audit test scripts
2. Add trace spans to the orchestrator and agents
3. Write the Playwright smoke test
4. Run, record and write up results
